SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which direction is directly opposite to north? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. South
   C. West
   D. North-east

2. How many cardinal points are there on a compass? (1 mark)
   A. Eight
   B. Two
   C. Four
   D. Six

3. On a map, the market is drawn above the school. Which direction is the market from the school? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. West
   C. South
   D. East

4. Lake Nakuru is famous for which birds? (1 mark)
   A. Owls
   B. Flamingos
   C. Ostriches
   D. Eagles

5. What do we call a place where a river falls over a cliff? (1 mark)
   A. Waterfall
   B. Plain
   C. Valley
   D. Plateau

6. Which season is best for planting most crops? (1 mark)
   A. Rainy season
   B. Dry season
   C. Hot season
   D. Cold season

7. Which drink is likely to sell more during the hot season? (1 mark)
   A. Hot porridge
   B. Hot tea
   C. Hot soup
   D. Cold drinks

8. Why is it dangerous to cross a flooded road? (1 mark)
   A. Water is always clean
   B. Water may be deep and fast and can hide holes
   C. There is no traffic
   D. The road is shorter

9. How can a historic place help a county to earn money? (1 mark)
   A. By stopping all jobs
   B. By selling its walls
   C. By closing to everybody
   D. By bringing visitors who pay fees and buy things

10. What is a museum? (1 mark)
   A. A bus stage
   B. A building where old objects are kept and shown
   C. A kind of factory
   D. A place where crops are grown

11. What does UNESCO do for important old places? (1 mark)
   A. Moves them to other countries
   B. Paints them
   C. Sells them
   D. Helps to protect them

12. Why do health workers depend on farmers? (1 mark)
   A. Farmers grow the food they eat
   B. Farmers build hospitals
   C. Farmers make medicine
   D. Farmers keep records

13. Which food is made of maize and beans mixed together? (1 mark)
   A. Githeri
   B. Chapati
   C. Mahamri
   D. Pilau

14. What is a motto? (1 mark)
   A. A school bag
   B. A school bell
   C. A class register
   D. A short sentence showing what a school stands for

15. What are school rules? (1 mark)
   A. Songs
   B. Instructions on what we should and should not do
   C. Lunch
   D. Games

16. Which words help to tell a history in order? (1 mark)
   A. Up, down, left
   B. Red, blue, green
   C. First, then, later, today
   D. Big, small, tall

17. What does conservation of resources mean? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring resources
   B. Wasting resources
   C. Using resources wisely and protecting them
   D. Selling everything at once

18. Which of these is a natural resource? (1 mark)
   A. A school building
   B. A tractor
   C. A road
   D. Water in a river

19. What is a resource? (1 mark)
   A. A game
   B. Something we can use to meet our needs and earn a living
   C. A school rule
   D. A kind of weather

20. Which industry uses milk as raw material? (1 mark)
   A. A dairy
   B. A shoe workshop
   C. A cement plant
   D. A sugar mill

21. What is a good thing to do at the end of a project? (1 mark)
   A. Forget about it
   B. Evaluate what went well and what to improve
   C. Throw away records
   D. Blame others

22. What is peace? (1 mark)
   A. Calm and harmony where people live safely and respect each other
   B. A game
   C. A kind of food
   D. A loud noise

23. Why is early marriage harmful? (1 mark)
   A. It helps children learn
   B. It stops education and harms health
   C. It makes children rich
   D. It is fun

24. Which is a responsibility of a child? (1 mark)
   A. Skip school
   B. Bully others
   C. Steal
   D. Respect others and study hard

25. Which is a way to promote child rights in school? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring children with problems
   B. Hiding problems
   C. Making posters and songs on child protection
   D. Bullying

26. What is a ballot paper? (1 mark)
   A. A ticket for a bus
   B. A kind of book
   C. A paper on which a voter marks a choice
   D. A menu

27. What does democracy mean? (1 mark)
   A. Rule by one person
   B. No rules
   C. Rule by force
   D. Rule by the people

28. What does the county executive do? (1 mark)
   A. Carries out the laws and runs county services
   B. Prints money
   C. Makes national laws
   D. Trains police

29. How many MCAs does each ward elect? (1 mark)
   A. One
   B. Ten
   C. Fifty
   D. None

30. How often are governors elected? (1 mark)
   A. Every year
   B. Every twenty years
   C. Every five years
   D. Every month

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Name the four in-between points on a compass and say between which cardinal points each lies. (4 marks)

32. Give two reasons why farmers plant crops at the start of the rainy season. (2 marks)

33. Describe what you should do if you are being bullied. (3 marks)

34. Explain how pollution can be reduced in an industry. (3 marks)

35. Explain why a ballot should be secret. (2 marks)

36. Explain why it is important to have a Children's Government in school. (4 marks)

37. Who is a clan elder? (2 marks)

38. Explain the difference between the size of a county and its population. (3 marks)

39. State three benefits of interdependence in a county. (3 marks)

40. Explain why buying votes with sweets is wrong. (3 marks)

41. Name four forms of child abuse. (4 marks)

42. List four democratic processes in a school. (4 marks)

43. Write a short poem of four lines about the benefits of industries in your county. (5 marks)

44. Explain why Kenya does not have summer and winter. (2 marks)

45. List four ways of caring for rivers and lakes. (4 marks)

46. Why do people trade? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — South
   North and south are opposite each other on the compass rose.

2. C — Four
   There are four cardinal points: north, east, south and west.

3. A — North
   Above means north when north is at the top.

4. B — Flamingos
   Lake Nakuru is well known for flamingos.

5. A — Waterfall
   A waterfall is where a river drops over a steep edge.

6. A — Rainy season
   Seeds need rain water to germinate and grow.

7. D — Cold drinks
   People are thirsty and feel hot, so they buy cold drinks.

8. B — Water may be deep and fast and can hide holes
   Floods can carry people and vehicles away.

9. D — By bringing visitors who pay fees and buy things
   Visitors spend money on tickets, guides and crafts.

10. B — A building where old objects are kept and shown
   Museums keep artefacts safely and show them to people.

11. D — Helps to protect them
   UNESCO names World Heritage Sites and helps to protect them.

12. A — Farmers grow the food they eat
   Everyone needs food, including nurses and doctors.

13. A — Githeri
   Githeri is maize and beans.

14. D — A short sentence showing what a school stands for
   A motto is a short saying of aims.

15. B — Instructions on what we should and should not do
   Rules guide behaviour.

16. C — First, then, later, today
   Time words link events in order.

17. C — Using resources wisely and protecting them
   Conservation keeps resources for the future.

18. D — Water in a river
   Water in a river is from nature.

19. B — Something we can use to meet our needs and earn a living
   Resources include land, water, minerals and people's skills.

20. A — A dairy
   Dairies process milk.

21. B — Evaluate what went well and what to improve
   Evaluation helps us do better next time.

22. A — Calm and harmony where people live safely and respect each other
   Peace is harmony and safety.

23. B — It stops education and harms health
   Early marriage harms girls and boys.

24. D — Respect others and study hard
   Rights come with responsibilities.

25. C — Making posters and songs on child protection
   Awareness helps protect children.

26. C — A paper on which a voter marks a choice
   Voters mark ballot papers.

27. D — Rule by the people
   Democracy means the people have a say.

28. A — Carries out the laws and runs county services
   The executive runs the county.

29. A — One
   Each ward elects one MCA.

30. C — Every five years
   General elections are held every five years.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: North-east (between north and east), south-east (between south and east), south-west (between south and west), north-west (between north and west).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct in-between point with its place.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: The rain gives the seeds water to grow, and the wet soil is soft to dig.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stay calm and do not fight back, walk away to a safe place, and tell a trusted adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Treat waste before releasing it, plant trees, and use clean machines or methods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: So that nobody can force or influence how a person votes, so the choice is free.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: It gives pupils a voice, teaches leadership, helps teachers with order and cleanliness, and teaches democracy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: A clan elder is an older respected member of a clan who leads it and keeps its customs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for respected older member, 1 mark for leading or keeping customs.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Size is the area of land a county covers. Population is the number of people who live there. A big county can have few people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for size, 1 mark for population, 1 mark for the difference or example.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: People get goods and services they cannot make, people help each other in trouble, and the county develops faster.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is cheating, it makes the election unfair, and votes should be given freely on merit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Early and forced marriage, female genital mutilation, child labour and child trafficking. Accept slavery, sexual abuse, abuse of children with special needs or unsafe transport.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each form.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Electing class monitors, class meetings, using a suggestion box, and voting on decisions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each process.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: A poem that mentions jobs, income and goods, is neat and rhymes or has rhythm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for four lines, 1 mark for jobs, 1 mark for income or goods, 1 mark for a title, 1 mark for correct language.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Kenya lies on the equator, so the temperature changes little through the year. Our seasons depend mainly on rain and on how high the land is.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the equator idea, 1 mark for rain or height.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not throw rubbish into them, plant trees on the banks, do not wash or farm too close to the water, and tell adults about pollution.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: People trade to get the goods they need but cannot make, and to earn money from the goods they produce.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.
